page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.48xlarge is an enterprise-grade general-purpose instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by 64-bit Intel x86 processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz, the server provides 96 physical cores configured with simultaneous multithreading to deliver 192 dedicated virtual CPUs. The compute subsystem is paired with 768.0 GB of system memory, upholding a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, reserving all chassis power, thermal headroom, and compute pathways exclusively for central processor tasks.

A primary differentiator of the m8idb.48xlarge configuration is its bundled storage and network capacity. The platform integrates 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage attached directly to the host system. This integrated solid-state capacity delivers ultra-low latency and substantial local I/O throughput without drawing from external storage networks. Complementing the local storage layer is a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation, enabling high-rate data transfers, rapid state synchronization across distributed topologies, and fluid ingestion of enterprise-scale network traffic.

From an efficiency standpoint, the consolidation of 192 vCPUs, 768 GB of RAM, and 11.4 TB of local NVMe SSDs within a single host envelope provides exceptionally dense throughput per deployed node. This integration mitigates the network overhead and separate capacity provisioning costs typical of standalone block storage architectures. An operational tradeoff is the ephemeral nature of the instance store volumes, which necessitates robust software-level replication or continuous external backup pipelines to protect against host-level interruptions. The hardware balance renders the m8idb.48xlarge optimal for massive relational databases, real-time search clusters, distributed analytics engines, high-volume transactional services, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.48xlarge is an enterprise general-purpose instance engineered on the AWS Nitro platform. It delivers 192 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs across 96 physical cores operating at 3.9 GHz, paired with 768.0 GB of memory to maintain a balanced 4:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance features 11,400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 200 Gbps baseline networking capacity. It contains no GPU accelerators, focusing all host resources on high-concurrency CPU operations and local storage I/O. The provision of dense local NVMe storage provides superior qualitative I/O cost efficiency compared to reliant external block storage, though workloads must account for the ephemeral nature of host-attached volumes. This configuration is best suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches requiring fast local persistence, distributed big data frameworks, and high-throughput transaction processing systems.
